title: tsdb: persist WAL truncation mint to fix minValidTime underestimation on restart
body:
## What this does

On restart, `Head.Init` computes `minValidTime` from `inOrderBlocksMaxTime`, the max time among on-disk blocks that don't carry the `FromSelectedSeries` or `FromStaleSeries` compaction hint. This can come back lower than where the WAL was actually truncated:
- A block written by `CompactSelectedSeries` or `CompactStaleHead` is deliberately excluded from that search, since it only ever covers part of a chunk range.
- A truncation whose range had nothing left to write (e.g. everything in it was already moved out by one of the above) never produces a block at all.

When the only blocks on disk are of that kind, `minValidTime` falls all the way back to `math.MinInt64`. WAL replay then no longer skips samples that are "before minValidTime", so it can walk into a leftover sample whose series record has already legitimately aged out of the checkpoint (its WAL expiry lapsed while the sample's own segment was still in the newest third of segments a checkpoint leaves untouched), and log it as an unknown series reference. No data is lost -- the sample's data is already durable in a block -- but the warning is spurious and can be misleading in practice.

## The fix

The `mint` a WAL truncation used is now carried inside the checkpoint itself, as a new WAL record type (`record.MinValidTime`).

- `wlog.Checkpoint` writes one such record, as the very first record of every checkpoint, holding the `mint` it was called with. It doesn't need to carry forward whatever the previous checkpoint recorded: `truncateWAL` only ever calls `Checkpoint` with a strictly increasing `mint`, so each checkpoint's own value is already the highest one that has ever existed. A copy absorbed from the previous checkpoint is dropped.
- `wlog.ReadMinValidTime(dir)` opens the most recent checkpoint and decodes this first record. It returns `ok == false` (no error) if there is no checkpoint yet, or if the most recent one predates this record (e.g. written by an older Prometheus version).
- On restart, `Open` reads that value back and uses `max(stored, computed-from-blocks)` for `minValidTime`, so it never regresses below a point the WAL was already truncated to, regardless of which (if any) blocks exist for that range.

This keeps the fix's durability tied to the checkpoint's own lifecycle instead of a separate file that could go stale relative to it. It is also naturally backward/forward compatible: an older checkpoint simply has no such record (falls back to today's behavior), and an older Prometheus version re-checkpointing a newer checkpoint will just drop the record it doesn't recognize on its next checkpoint, same fallback.

One rollout caveat: this only protects a restart after at least one checkpoint has run under the fixed binary. A checkpoint written before the upgrade has no `MinValidTime` record, so a restart before that point still falls back to the old (buggy) computation.

## Testing

- `TestCompactSelectedSeries_RestartReplaysOrphanedSampleAsUnknownSeriesRef` (`tsdb/db_test.go`): end-to-end regression test -- evicts a series via `CompactSelectedSeries`, forces two WAL checkpoints so the series record ages out of the checkpoint while a leftover sample survives in an unrewritten segment, then restarts the DB and asserts WAL replay reports zero unknown series references.
- `TestRecord_MinValidTime` / `TestRecord_MinValidTimeDecodeWrongType` (`tsdb/record/record_test.go`): encode/decode round-trip and invalid-type error.
- `TestReadMinValidTime_NoCheckpointYet` / `_AfterCheckpoint` / `_ReflectsOnlyLatestCheckpoint` / `_OlderCheckpointWithoutRecord` (`tsdb/wlog/checkpoint_test.go`): `ReadMinValidTime` against real checkpoints written by `Checkpoint`.
- `go test ./tsdb/...` passes in full. Fixed along the way: `tsdb/agent`'s WAL replay treated any unrecognized record type as corruption and needed to tolerate this new one, since the agent also writes its checkpoints via `wlog.Checkpoint`; a few existing tests that assert exact checkpoint content (`readTestWAL` and friends) needed to skip over the new record too.
